limits.chordBody: A channel sounds one note at a time, so a chord needs a channel for each of its notes.
limits.chordFix: Play the chord as a fast arpeggio on one channel, the sound the era is known for, or choose the arpeggio behaviour and let a part cycle through its notes.
limits.fmBody: When the sample channel is on it takes FM channel six, so a song with drum samples has five FM channels left. Green Hill Zone does exactly that: its drums are samples written at about 15.4 kHz, and the melody, bass and chords share the other five.
limits.fmFix: Write the arrangement for five FM channels as soon as there are samples in it, and give the drums to the sample channel.
limits.fmTitle: Six FM channels, and the sixth is the sample channel
limits.intro: The Mega Drive makes its music with a YM2612, six FM channels and a sample channel, and a PSG, three square channels and a noise channel. Each limit below comes with the way the music of the time worked around it, Sonic the Hedgehog first among them.
limits.levelBody: An FM operator's level moves in steps of 0.75 dB, and a square's in steps of 2 dB, with sixteen levels and the last of them silence.
limits.levelFix: Give smooth fades to the FM channels, and on the squares fade quickly enough that the steps pass before they are heard.
limits.lfoBody: There is a single low frequency oscillator, so every channel's vibrato and tremolo runs at the same speed. A channel only chooses how much of each it takes.
limits.lfoFix: Write vibrato as pitch changes instead. Marble Zone writes 884 frequency changes in thirty seconds, which lets each part wobble at its own speed, and a pitch automation lane does the same.
limits.lfoTitle: One LFO for the whole chip
limits.panBody: An FM channel plays left, right or both, with nothing in between, and the squares and the noise have no stereo at all on a standard console.
limits.panFix: Place parts hard left, hard right or in the middle, and for width double a part on a second channel, quieter, on the other side.
limits.releaseBody: Some drivers never let a release sound. Mickey Mania keys the next note on straight after the last one ends and writes silence for a rest, so its patches keep a release that never fades.
limits.releaseFix: When a patch taken from a game rings on after its note, raise its release rate.
limits.releaseTitle: A release that is never heard
limits.sampleBody: Every sample is stored in the cartridge, and an XGM resamples them to 14000 Hz, keeps 63 of them and mixes at most four at once. Sonic the Hedgehog's four drum hits, recovered from a recording of the soundtrack, come to 40,744 bytes.
limits.sampleFix: Keep hits short and their rate low, and play one hit at another pitch rather than storing a second.
limits.squareBody: The square channels go no lower than about 109 Hz, a little below A2, and the noise channel has only three speeds of its own.
limits.squareFix: Leave the bass to FM. For a tuned noise, such as a pitched snare, silence the third square and let the noise take its pitch.
limits.squareTitle: Three squares and a noise channel
limits.threeBody: Channel three has a mode that gives each of its four operators a pitch of its own.
limits.threeFix: Use it for a chord, a detuned unison or an effect that would otherwise take several channels.
limits.threeTitle: Channel three can play four notes
